G2 partial-fail — the 2026-07-09 board authorization of a $500M buyback through 2028 is discretionary capacity, not a concrete commitment to buy, and it was already announced (stock fell anyway). verified.primary_source: EquipmentShare IPO pricing release, equipmentshare.com (2026-01-22, $24.50 / 30.5M shares); MarketBeat lock-up alert (2026-07-15, expiry 2026-07-22); GlobeNewswire buyback + guidance raise (2026-07-09); FMP quote $16.615 (2026-07-20)
verified.analysis: The dated fact checks out: EquipmentShare IPO'd 2026-01-23 at $24.50 with only 30.5M shares floated, and the lock-up expires 2026-07-22 — hard-dated, forward, not yet fired. But the mechanism fails strict gating: this is a supply/technical event, not a value-unlock with a named counterparty or an unpriced commitment, and it has been broadly telegraphed while the stock already de-rated to $16.62 (yearLow $15.95), which is the market pre-discounting the overhang rather than ignoring it. The $500M buyback authorized 2026-07-09 alongside a raised FY26 outlook (revenue $5.25-5.68B, adj. core EBITDA $1.95-2.06B) is the only real company-side offset, and it is discretionary capacity already announced and already sold into — so the residual forward edge is a reflexive timing bet on the shape of the flush, which is exactly what the triage note concedes. Gap: I did not confirm the exact releasable share count or any early-release/staged-tranche provisions from the S-1 lock-up language, which would be the one thing that could reintroduce a genuine G3 figure.

verified.analysis: The catalyst is real, specific, dated and forward: a signed definitive agreement (07/06/26) with fixed consideration and remaining hard gates (S-4 effectiveness, two shareholder votes, HSR and foreign antitrust) targeting a 1H-2027 close, so the process milestones have not fired. The problem is economics, not existence: 75% of the consideration is SOLS stock and SOLS has fallen from a $90.80 52-week high to $58.38 (26% below its 50d average), so unhedged ESI is effectively a levered directional bet on Solstice rather than a spread capture, while the hedged spread is only ~4.8% gross over roughly ten months. Gap to note: I could not confirm the S-4 is on file or any special-meeting date, so the next hard dated checkpoint is inferred rather than sourced, and no unpriced G3 figure (e.g., synergy or divestiture detail beyond the disclosed >$180M run-rate) was verifiable in this budget - hence WATCH pending S-4 filing.

verified.edge: H — announcement dated 2026-04-30 has visibly NOT re-rated the equity: FIP trades $4.16 vs 52wk high $7.94 and 52wk low $3.90, below the 50d ($4.57) and 200d ($5.11) averages, i.e. the market is discounting closing/regulatory risk and residual rail-segment weakness rather than pricing >$300M of net proceeds against a $492M cap.
verified.primary_source: FTAI Infrastructure press release / 8-K, "FTAI Infrastructure Inc. Announces Agreement to Sell Long Ridge Energy and Power to MARA Holdings, Inc.", ir.fipinc.com and GlobeNewswire, 2026-04-30; plus Q1 2026 earnings call commentary (2026-05-08) guiding FERC approval to mid-Q3 2026; price data FMP quote 2026-07-20 ($4.16, mcap $492M)
verified.kill_fact: Core catalyst survives primary-source check and is still FORWARD: FTAI Infrastructure's 2026-04-30 press release (globenewswire/ir.fipinc, Skadden confirmation) states a definitive agreement to sell Long Ridge Energy & Power to a MARA Holdings subsidiary for ~$1.52B ($1.512B pre-adjustment), eliminating $1.16B of Long Ridge debt and using net proceeds to repay ~$300M of parent debt, expected to close in Q3 2026 subject to regulatory approvals; no closing announcement exists as of 2026-07-20, so the event has not fired. Tape is consistent with an unpriced event: FIP $4.16, mkt cap $492M, 52wk low $3.90 / high $7.94, below 50d ($4.57) and 200d ($5.11). CORRECTIONS: (1) the condition set is overstated — the filings name FERC Section 203 change-of-control as the operative approval plus customary conditions; STB (Surface Transportation Board) clearance is NOT a condition of this power/gas asset sale and appears fabricated (STB relates to the retained Transtar rail business, not Long Ridge), and HSR is not separately confirmed; (2) 'mid-Q3 2026', the ~$30M/yr interest savings, and the 9.5x-to-7.4x leverage step with a 5.1x target are management commentary from the Q1 call, not press-release facts, and could not be independently re-verified; (3) FERC 203 timing is the live risk — no docket outcome confirmable, and a Q3 slip is the base failure mode. Residual thesis weakness stands as stated: post-close equity is a levered, still-lossmaking Transtar/Jefferson/Repauno story, so the sale de-risks the balance sheet without proving the remainco earns its cost of capital.
verified.analysis: The catalyst is verified real, specific, dated and still forward: a signed definitive agreement (2026-04-30) with a named public counterparty, with closing conditioned on FERC 203, HSR and STB clearances and guided to mid-Q3 2026, so the structural deleveraging event has not yet occurred. The unpriced element is the capital-structure step change — $1.16B of Long Ridge debt leaves the balance sheet, >$300M of net proceeds retires parent debt, corporate leverage drops 9.5x to 7.4x with a 5.1x target — set against a market cap of only ~$492M and a share price sitting near its 52-week low, which is not the tape of a re-rated event. Main gaps in this focused check: I could not confirm from public sources whether the FERC/HSR filings have already cleared as of 2026-07-20, and the residual entity is a leveraged, still-loss-making freight-rail/terminal business, so the post-close equity value depends on Transtar/Jefferson/Repauno execution rather than on the sale alone.
